debates.crux: How deeply did Pico understand Kabbalah?
debates.importance: Critical for assessing Pico's syncretism claims

scholars.Wirszubski: Genuine synthesis; Pico read the texts carefully and understood Sefirotic structure
scholars.Kristeller: Supports Wirszubski; documents Pico's access to Kabbalistic texts
scholars.Busi: Mixed; strong on Sefirotic correspondence, weak on practical Kabbalah
scholars.Allen: Pico understood Kabbalah selectively; emphasized Neoplatonic layer over authentic mysticism

evidence.key_indicator: Explicit Kabbalistic doctrine (binsica, letter permutation, Sefirotic correspondences)
Layer 5 Kabbalistic interpretation of Genesis; shows systematic Sefirotic reading

debates.assessment: Preponderance of evidence supports Wirszubski: Pico engaged seriously with Kabbalah, demonstrated genuine understanding of Sefirotic system, though may have adapted rather than strictly adhered to Lurianic tradition.

debates.crux: Is Heptaplus literal Biblical exegesis or Neoplatonic cosmology with Biblical labels?
debates.importance: Determines how to read Pico's hermeneutical method

scholars.Black: Both - Pico genuinely attempting to reconcile textual authority with philosophical principle
scholars.Howlett: More reconciliation attempt than pure exegesis; Pico is straining the text
scholars.Allen: More Ficino Platonism than Pico's own innovation; dependent on Ficino's Platonic Theology

evidence.key_indicator: Systematic seven-layer hermeneutics; each layer (literal, allegorical, tropological, anagogical, Kabbalistic, astrological, numerological) treats same text as different philosophical principle

debates.assessment: Black and Howlett are both correct: Pico intends genuine exegesis but within a philosophical framework that determines interpretation. The point is not textual archaeology but doctrinal harmony - whether all philosophical traditions (Pseudo-Dionysius, Aquinas, Kabbalah, Plotinus) describe the same cosmic truth.

debates.crux: Did Pico reject Aquinas or deepen his synthesis?
debates.importance: Establishes whether Pico is scholastic reformer or revolutionary

scholars.Edelheit: Deepens - uses Aquinas as foundation, modifies via Neoplatonic participation
scholars.Howlett: Deepens with tension - strains Aquinas's framework but within scholastic method
scholars.Some scholasticists: Incoherent synthesis; Plotinus + Kabbalah cannot cohere with Aquinas

evidence.key_indicator: Explicit dialogue with Aristotle + Plotinus; maintains Aquinas's being/essence doctrine while importing Plotinian emanation
Angels as participatory intelligences - Aquinas framework applied to mystical union (Plotinian eros)

debates.assessment: Edelheit is most accurate: Pico deepens Aquinas by importing Plotinian participation and Kabbalistic mysticism. The synthesis works at the level of metaphysics (all hierarchies are participatory) even where individual doctrines seem to diverge.

debates.crux: Is angelology central to Pico's heretical status (1486 Rome trial)?
debates.importance: Determines which angelology conclusions were condemned

scholars.Copenhaver: Yes - celestial magic (section 5 of 900 Conclusions) depends on angelology; condemned for attempting demonic invocation through angelic names
scholars.Farmer: Yes - Goetia correspondences (72 spirits) as demonic beings, not angels
scholars.Howlett: Partly - the freedom/dignity thesis (based on angelic fixed nature vs. human freedom) was heretical

evidence.key_indicator: Explicit invocations of celestial/planetary angels; possible demonic summoning interpretation

debates.assessment: Copenhaver and Farmer are correct: angelology was central to heretical condemna tions, particularly around demonic invocation via celestial names and Kabbalistic summoning.
